source_spans.locator: Neuroscience 139(1), published p.201 / PDF p.1, abstract and introduction: the two familiar source constructs each comprise dissociable phenomena; selection operates at perceptual and postperceptual stages and maintenance mechanisms differ by information type

Neuroscience 139(1), published pp.202-203 / PDF pp.2-3, late-selection evidence: goal-driven selection determines which already perceptually and semantically processed items gain access to the severely capacity-limited online store

Neuroscience 139(1), published pp.204-205 / PDF pp.4-5, delay-period spatial-maintenance evidence: interrupting or redirecting spatial selection away from remembered locations selectively impairs retention, while the authors caution against generalizing the same relation to all maintained information

Neuroscience 139(1), published p.207 / PDF p.7, Conclusions: the relationship is explicitly characterized as multifaceted, with distinct gatekeeping, active-maintenance, and executive-manipulation interactions and unresolved boundaries across information types

conditions: goal-directed visual processing in which selection can operate at multiple processing stages and the active-maintenance system can retain different kinds of information by functionally dissociable mechanisms
substrate: visual information-processing and capacity-limited active-maintenance systems
task: prioritize behaviorally relevant visual information for processing or storage and maintain or manipulate selected representations
temporal_scope: interaction modes span early sensory processing, later admission to an online store, delay-period maintenance, and active manipulation or updating

nodes.description: a particular form of goal-directed selection distinguished by the stage or operation at which it influences processing
a particular active-maintenance mechanism distinguished by the kind of information maintained or the operation performed on stored representations
distinction among early sensory selection, postperceptual admission control, delay-period maintenance-related selection, and executive manipulation or updating
distinction among different kinds of maintained information for which the source reports or leaves open functionally different maintenance-selection relations
the specific functional relation observed between a selection subtype and an active-maintenance subtype in a given task

relations.description: selection effects must be distinguished by the processing stage or operation at which they occur rather than treated as one unitary mechanism
active-maintenance mechanisms and their interaction with selection differ with the kind of information or maintenance operation under consideration
the nature of the observed interaction depends on which selection process and which active-maintenance process are instantiated in the task
